key_insight: A first-principles-trained neural network potential predicts oxygen-vacancy migration in SrTiO₃ with an enthalpy of 0.64 eV, close to the experimental 0.67 eV.
engineering_relevance: The model enables larger, longer simulations of defect transport in perovskite oxides, potentially informing materials engineering rather than directly demonstrating improved solar-cell performance.
method: Train a neural network potential on ab initio molecular dynamics data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO₃.
Validate energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies against DFT references.
Run large-scale, long-time molecular dynamics and extract vacancy diffusion coefficients and migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces DFT reference properties and supercell-size trends, while its vacancy diffusion coefficients agree better with experiment than conventional classical MD results.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the sampled SrTiO₃ configurations and defect conditions requires additional validation.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
